messages:
sam_sales: FYI deepwater POC hitting variable TTFTs and occasional 429s, started after they ramped concurrency to 12. Logs show a bunch of cache miss + prefetch timeouts. Can we swarm?
nia_eng: copying in kevin_sre and alex_platform. any recent routing/prefetch changes?
kevin_sre: I see a surge to 12 concurrent sessions, our shard affinity caused queueing + some batch window growth. grabbing logs now.
marie_support: customer report: median first token ~450ms -> sometimes 1.2s, and ~2% 429s. they rely on Prefetch policy = aggressive.
alex_platform: no infra deploys in last 6h. we did tweak prefetch backpressure thresholds in staging yesterday but not prod.
opsbot: [alert] prefetch-timeout spike on shard s-03 (2024-03-18T11:02:14Z)
kevin_sre: past hour: prefetch queue length increased from 8->24 on s-03 when their concurrency ramped. that causes continuous batching to expand sequence and raises TTFT.
nia_eng: can you paste a short snippet of the relevant logs?
kevin_sre: ```
[2024-03-18T11:02:14Z] shard=s-03 req=deepwater-42 action=prefetch timeout_ms=250 err="prefetch timeout, kvcache miss"
[2024-03-18T11:02:14Z] shard=s-03 req=deepwater-43 batch_size=6 latency_first_token_ms=1143
[2024-03-18T11:02:15Z] shard=s-03 err=429 msg="route throttle" capacity=0
```
sam_sales: ok that matches what customer saw. they're running a single model variant pinned to 8-bit quant.
alex_platform: 8-bit quant shouldn't trigger this alone. likely batching/backpressure interacting with prefetch misses (KV cache cold for this workload).
anna_security: (anna_security) quick Q: any customer data leakage risk while we change prefetch/policy? want to be sure config changes keep same VPC controls.
marie_support: no config changes to networking. we'll only adjust prefetch/backoff and warmup policy. no data plane changes.
kevin_sre: immediate mitigation suggestions: reduce customer concurrency to 6 (temp), set prefetch backoff to linear 50ms->200ms, and enable aggressive KV prefill for this tenant for next 10m. also throttle batch window max to 8 to avoid runaway grouping.
nia_eng: prefer to flip a tenant override: 
```
tenant_overrides:
  deepwater:
    prefetch_backoff_ms: 50
    prefill_kv:true
    max_batch_size: 8
```
kevin_sre: will apply override to staging, smoke, then prod (small window). I can do a rolling change to s-03 first.
sam_sales: customer ok with a short change as long as we monitor and revert if any auth/latency regression. they're on a trial and ask about pricing impact if we increase prefill.
alex_platform: prefill will add small read/warmup cost on our side but hardly affects their billed tokens. we can recommend short warmup windows and revert. estimate +1-3% infra cost for the POC.
marie_support: i'll tell customer the plan and ask them to hold concurrency while we flip.
kevin_sre: flipping override to prod on s-03 in 2m, will post updates.
opsbot: [deploy] tenant override applied to s-03 (rollout id: ro-7731)
kevin_sre: done on s-03. monitoring TTFT and 429 rate.
kevin_sre: initial metrics look better: median first token down from ~450ms -> ~180ms on s-03, 429s dropped to 0.4%
marie_support: customer confirms improvement on their side. they will slowly ramp concurrency and report.
sam_sales: great — can we capture this as a recommended prefill + batch window doc for presales? we'll want a short blurb in the sales playbook.
nia_eng: I'll draft a one-pager with recommended tenant overrides, cost estimate, and rollback steps. cc alex_platform for prod-safe knobs.
anna_security: please include note: all changes are tenant-scoped, no network or KMS changes. I'll sign off once draft ready.
sam_sales: thanks team. small follow-up: they asked about SLA impact if they go multi-shard — any blockers?
alex_platform: multi-shard helps throughput but requires warmup for KV caches; we should prefill target shards when adding capacity. also set consistent routing to avoid hot-shard fanout.
kevin_sre: agree. will outline a migration checklist for the customer POC.
marie_support: closing the immediate swarm. will reopen if anything else pops. :thumbsup:
